headline_notes: Every KL is KL(model || program) per token on HELD text, 512 rows x 256 tokens = 131,072 tokens, tables fitted on 24,576 est rows (6.29M positions). The `kl_at_finding23_setting` column is the same quantity on the 96 x 256 = 24,576-token slice tf_interp3.ladder_v uses, so it is directly comparable to FINDING 23.

Bits: 32 per table entry, and 32 per model parameter with the tied embedding counted once.  Measured 8-bit quantisation of the top-stage program costs <0.0004 nats, so every program bill can be divided by ~4 at negligible KL; the model quantises just as well, so the ORDERING of program vs model is unchanged by quantisation.

The model is still the shortest description of itself: at 8 bits per parameter it reaches KL 0.0004-0.0008 at 0.32-6.92 MB, and no program point is both shorter and comparable in KL.  What the program beats is the BIGRAM BASELINE, at strictly fewer bits, at all three cells.
